title: Deadlock
description: Learn about deadlocks and how they occur in SQL Server.

data.text: A deadlock is a concurrency problem where two sessions block each other's progress. Each session holds a lock on a resource the other session needs.
In a deadlock, SQL Server proactively terminates one of the sessions. The terminated session is called the deadlock victim.
Two sessions access the same tables in different orders:

rows: UPDATE invoices SET customer_id = 100 WHERE id = 1
UPDATE invoice_items SET amount = 100 WHERE id = 10
UPDATE invoice_items SET item_name = 'Cool Keyboard' WHERE id = 10 — Blocked
UPDATE invoices SET total = ... WHERE id = 1 — Blocked

data.title: Deadlock Key Points
points: Deadlocks occur when two sessions lock resources the other needs.
SQL Server chooses one session as the deadlock victim.
Design applications to access tables in a consistent order to prevent deadlocks.
The deadlock victim receives an error message and must retry the transaction.
